prompt.context: Over the past five years, the government of Saudi Arabia has been focused on reducing economic dependence on oil by diversifying the domestic economy. As part of this effort, the government has evidenced a willingness to relax certain social norms. As part of the diversification initiative, the government hired us to forecast the potential revenue impact of taxing shisha consumption.
prompt.question: What is the estimated revenue impact of legalizing and taxing public shisha consumption in Saudi Arabia over a three-year period?

clarifying_info.a: Shisha is an instrument for vaporizing and smoking flavored tobacco. In the Arab world and Middle East, people smoke waterpipes as part of the cultural traditions.

clarifying_info.q: How will the Saudi government make money off of shisha?
clarifying_info.a: Institutions must apply and pay for an annual license to sell shisha. Additionally, sales tax and import tariffs are levied by the government as appropriate.

clarifying_info.q: Is there a specific revenue target in mind?
clarifying_info.a: No, the Saudi government only wishes to maximize revenue over a 3-year period.

clarifying_info.q: How much revenue does the Saudi government currently earn?
clarifying_info.a: 2.5 trillion Saudi riyal annually. Tobacco and other related products currently generate 500 million SAR in revenue.

clarifying_info.q: Are there any social norms we should be aware of?
clarifying_info.a: Islam is widely practiced by Saudi citizens and governs their personal, political, economic and legal lives. Additionally, public consumption of shisha is currently banned but is widely consumed at home.

framework: Revenue Sources: (1) License fees — type/quantity of businesses, one-time vs. annual structure, adoption rate over 3 years; (2) Sales tax — consumer segments, public adoption rate, tax rate; (3) Import tariffs — domestic vs. foreign sourced shisha, tariff percentage
Cost Considerations: regulatory body setup, auditing and quality control, implementation vs. ongoing costs
Social Issues: public opinion on legalization, health and well-being of citizens, job creation potential

questions.prompt: Which licensing structure should Saudi Arabia adopt, and what is the estimated three-year revenue impact from licenses?
questions.guidance: Candidate should first compare the three license structures over a 3-year horizon per business to identify Jordan's structure as the revenue-maximizing option (21,000 SAR vs Qatar 10,000 vs UAE 15,000). Then apply Jordan's structure to the Riyadh restaurant market with 5% / 10% / 15% adoption rates in years 1/2/3, add 1,000 new restaurants per year for years 1 and 2, scale Riyadh results to national by dividing by 20%, and sum all three years. Great candidates will contextualize the result: the initiative adds ~17.1% to current tobacco-related revenue (500M SAR).

math.setup: Step 1 — Choose license structure by comparing 3-year total per business: Qatar (one-time 10k) = 10,000; Jordan (3k one-time + 500/mo = 6k/yr) = 3k + 6k + 6k + 6k = 21,000; UAE (6k one-time + 3k/yr) = 6k + 3k + 3k + 3k = 15,000. Jordan maximizes revenue. Step 2 — Build Riyadh restaurant count: Year 1 = 14,000; Year 2 = 15,000; Year 3 = 16,000 (1,000 new each year). Step 3 — Apply adoption rates to get participating restaurants and newly participating restaurants each year. Step 4 — Compute one-time fee revenue (3,000 SAR × newly participating) and annual fee revenue (500 SAR × 12 = 6,000 SAR × total participating). Step 5 — Scale to national by dividing Riyadh by 20% (multiply by 5). Step 6 — Sum three years.
steps: Year 1: 14,000 × 5% = 700 total participating; 700 newly participating; one-time = 700 × 3,000 = 2.1M SAR; annual = 700 × 6,000 = 4.2M SAR; Year 1 Riyadh total = 6.3M SAR
Year 2: 15,000 × 10% = 1,500 total participating; 800 newly participating; one-time = 800 × 3,000 = 2.4M SAR; annual = 1,500 × 6,000 = 9.0M SAR; Year 2 Riyadh total = 11.4M SAR
Year 3: 16,000 × 15% = 2,400 total participating; 900 newly participating; one-time = 900 × 3,000 = 2.7M SAR; annual = 2,400 × 6,000 = 14.4M SAR; Year 3 Riyadh total = 17.1M SAR
Scale to national: 34.8M ÷ 20% = 174M SAR total; or Year 3 run-rate national: 17.1M ÷ 20% = 85.5M SAR
Context: 85.5M SAR Year 3 run-rate vs. current 500M SAR tobacco revenue = ~17.1% increase
math.answer: Jordan's license structure maximizes 3-year revenue at 21,000 SAR per business. Estimated 3-year national license revenue is approximately 174M SAR; the Year 3 annual run-rate alone is 85.5M SAR, representing a ~17.1% increase over current tobacco-related revenue of 500M SAR.

brainstorming.prompt: Are there any other considerations the Saudi government should keep in mind before legalizing the public consumption of shisha?

categories.name: Health & Social Well-being
ideas: Health and well-being of citizens given increased consumption of tobacco products
Public opinion — restaurants may not want to sell shisha and patrons may not want to smoke in public

categories.name: Revenue Beyond Licenses
ideas: Revenues related to sales tax on shisha purchases
Import tariffs on foreign-sourced shisha products

categories.name: Costs & Implementation
ideas: Associated costs with launching and governing the program
Regulatory body setup and auditing / quality control expenses

categories.name: Distribution & Industry
ideas: Other distribution channels to sell shisha beyond restaurants (e.g., specialty shops, hotels)
Job creation related to the budding shisha industry

categories.name: Macroeconomic & Reputational
ideas: Three-year economic forecast and sustainability of revenue
Reputation on the global stage — many countries are restricting tobacco products

recommendation: Saudi Arabia should adopt Jordan's licensing structure (3,000 SAR one-time fee + 500 SAR monthly) as it maximizes 3-year per-business revenue at 21,000 SAR versus 10,000 (Qatar) and 15,000 (UAE).

Estimated national 3-year license revenue is approximately 174M SAR, with a Year 3 annual run-rate of 85.5M SAR — roughly a 17.1% increase on current tobacco-related government revenue of 500M SAR. Note: figures are conservative as they exclude sales tax and import tariff revenue.
risks: License revenue is highly sensitive to the assumed adoption rate; lower-than-expected restaurant participation would significantly reduce projections.
Increased tobacco consumption may raise healthcare costs, partially or fully offsetting revenue gains.
next_steps: Conduct market research on restaurants' willingness to sell shisha to validate and refine the adoption rate assumption.
Quantify financial and social costs associated with the program (regulatory setup, enforcement, public health impact) to determine net benefit.
Model incremental revenue from sales tax and import tariffs to develop a more complete revenue picture.
